1242 Mean, Variance, Expected Frequency of Binomial Distributions

examples.question_text: $X\sim\mathrm{Bin}(32,0.25)$. Find $E(X)$, $\mathrm{Var}(X)$ and $\sigma(X)$, giving the standard deviation correct to two decimal places.

A student guesses independently on each of $50$ multiple-choice questions. Each question has five options, with one correct answer. Let $X$ be the number answered correctly. Find the mean, variance and standard deviation of $X$, giving the standard deviation correct to two decimal places.
examples.solution_text:
Success: a question is answered correctly. There are $50$ independent trials, each with success probability $\frac15$.

$X\sim\mathrm{Bin}(50,0.2)$.

$\begin{aligned} E(X)&=np\\ &=50(0.2)\\ &=10 \end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned} \mathrm{Var}(X)&=np(1-p)\\ &=50(0.2)(0.8)\\ &=8 \end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned} \sigma(X)&=\sqrt{8}\\ &\approx2.83 \end{aligned}$

On average, the student answers $10$ questions correctly.

$np=18$ and $np(1-p)=7.2$.

Divide the variance by the mean:

$\begin{aligned} 1-p&=\frac{\mathrm{Var}(X)}{E(X)}\\ &=\frac{7.2}{18}\\ &=0.4 \end{aligned}$

$p=0.6$.

$\begin{aligned} n&=\frac{E(X)}{p}\\ &=\frac{18}{0.6}\\ &=30 \end{aligned}$

Thus $n=30$ and $p=0.6$.

examples.derivation: Using the source formulae: E(X)=32×0.25=8; Var(X)=32×0.25×0.75=6; σ(X)=√6=2.449489…≈2.45. The aligned equations have explicit left-hand sides, so no phantom equals gutter is required. No diagram is needed.

A correct guess has probability 1/5=0.2. Fifty independent guesses give X∼Bin(50,0.2). E(X)=50×0.2=10; Var(X)=50×0.2×0.8=8; σ(X)=√8=2.828427…≈2.83. The interpretation of the mean is correct. Prose remains editable outside mathematics; no diagram or phantom gutter is needed.

Since np=18>0, dividing np(1−p)=7.2 by np=18 gives 1−p=0.4, hence p=0.6 and n=18/0.6=30. Substitution confirms mean 30×0.6=18 and variance 30×0.6×0.4=7.2. This adapts source Guided Practice part d. No diagram or phantom gutter is needed.
